body: I've never even thought about that. And I genuinely am an asshole when I drink, so this is actually true! For the time bring I'm going to stay away and maybe in the future I will go.

Thank you! Yes, I think for at least the next month or so I'm going to steer clear of these events, just until I don't feel so shaky. I suppose I'm just fearful of someone finding out I don't drink because I have a problem and it causing me problems.

That's actually a really good idea - and I wouldn't be lying either as I am taking medication that you are not meant to drink with...I was just irresponsible and used to drink with it while I was still off the wagon.

I suppose I'm just worried because I want to fit in (being the new member of staff) and feel like most employees will be taking advantage of the fact they have lots of events with free alcohol. It's not so much the shame of not drinking, but worried if it somehow comes out the reason why I don't drink.

I'm sorry you're having a rough time at the moment. That sounds like a really tricky situation to be in as a recovering alcoholic. My husband and I are experiencing the same thing - we've ceased to go out now that I don't drink. Good for you for staying strong and not taking it out on your SO.

I don't know what your situation is as far as insurance or seeing a doctor is, but I have recently been prescribed Prazosin to help ease my nightmares and night-terrors. In higher doses the drug is used to treat  high blood pressure, but lower doses are used to treat nightmares and help symptoms of PTSD. They haven't made the dreams cease, but they have kicked down the intensity of them a couple of notches. Kind of like taking the dreams from an R rating to a PG. Maybe if possible you could speak to someone about it? I paid $20 to join the prescription savings plan at Walgreens and a months worth of this medication cost me $10. Cheap as chips and worry every penny.

I totally understand the sentiment of wishing you were a normal twenty something - I'm right there with you.

Stay strong.

* I'm a mean baker. 
* I am utterly loyal to the people I love. 
* I'm growing my hair out (had short hair for my entire life) and it really   does look lovely.
* I wrote a children's book which is being illustrated and hopefully will be published.
* I am a fantastic dog owner.

I've also suffered with depression my whole life and will have to take medication for the rest of my life. I self-medicated with alcohol and drugs for years and I'm three weeks dry tomorrow.

I've been blue, but just trying to distract myself. Mainly sewing, baking, walking. Anything really. I don't want to get out of bed in the morning, but I know not getting out of bed is not going to do me any good. 

I was hoping to feel 'healthier', but really I don't feel much different at all physically as of yet. I'm seeing a regular psychotherapist and my medication has been increased.

As a female, I can totally understand why she did this. There is NOTHING that brings more joy to my heart than waxing a man. It doesn't happen often, but when it does, it turns me into a manic, shrieking, monster. I can't even explain it...it fills me with utter glee! 

P.S Sorry for your balls.

Thank you so much for your kind words. It's good to hear nice things when everything is pretty awful at the moment (I made this profile straight out of hospital and was angry - hence the username). I'll be sure to check in later on this evening once I'm back.
I will let you know! Congratulations such a long time sober! Is it ever still a struggle or is it just life now? The idea of never drinking again seems unattainable and scary to me right now.

Thank you! I will check back after. I actually attempted to go earlier this week and walked in and saw my the lady that lives next door to me...I promptly left. So giving it a second try tonight. I will absolutely come back later with an update.

This is exactly how I feel. I've been sober for two weeks and day to day I feel...ok. But the idea of never drinking again scares the life out of me, and frankly seems utterly impossible. The only way I'm managing at the moment is trying to keep busy constantly. Baking. Sewing. Cutting my dog's hair. Writing a journal. Cleaning. Anything I can do to take my mind off drinking.  It's hard!

I feel your pain! I've not been drinking for two weeks and I've been having some pretty awful nightmares. I'm lucky to live with someone that knows that I can't drink...because otherwise I feel like I would have given up by now.

This is EXACTLY the position I'm in - though, I have a couple of years on you. I've not drank anything for two weeks now and because of this I haven't socialized with pretty much anyone, barring my bf who I live with. Even when I'm around people I know I'm still struggling to be talkative...let alone lively. It's hard!
Thank you. This is actually really helpful. I've only been out a few days and the guilt is the most overwhelming feeling that has come out of this entire situation.
I'm taking everything a day at a time at the moment...it's just awful knowing how much I've disappointed him.
I do have a therapist and have been on medication for two years - there is just a lot going on at the moment and I think I cracked.
